candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: use appropriate PPE and occupational/infection-prevention practices to protect healthcare personnel
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — respiratory protection program / respirator safety
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize medical evaluation, fit testing, and training as core OSHA respiratory protection requirements when workers are required to use tight-fitting respirators.

options.A: Medical evaluation, fit testing, and respirator training
options.B: Respirator distribution only, with no medical evaluation or training
options.C: Fit testing only after a worker reports a respiratory exposure
options.D: Training only, without evaluating whether the worker can medically use the respirator

candidate.rationale: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.134 requires a written respiratory protection program for required respirator use. Applicable program elements include medical evaluation of employees required to use respirators, fit testing for tight-fitting respirators, and training on respiratory hazards and proper respirator use. Medical evaluation occurs before fit testing or required workplace use. Therefore A is correct; the other options omit required program elements or delay them until after exposure.
candidate.source_claim_supported: When respirator use is required, OSHA requires an employer respiratory protection program that includes medical evaluation, fit testing for tight-fitting respirators, and training, among other applicable elements.
candidate.source_locator: 29 CFR 1910.134(c)(1)(ii)-(iii),(vii)-(ix) Respiratory Protection Program; §1910.134(e)(1) Medical Evaluation; §1910.134(f) Fit Testing; §1910.134(k) Training and Information
candidate.stem: Healthcare workers are required to use tight-fitting respirators because of a workplace respiratory hazard. Which elements are part of the employer's OSHA respiratory protection program?
